comment: The Learning Center curriculum — net-new, deep CONCEPTUAL lessons for people with no technical foundation (managers, marketers, vibe-coders, people building with Claude). NOT the docs. Each lesson teaches one big idea thoroughly, jargon-light, and links out to the deep doc pages (web/learn/<doc>.html) for the literals. Depth = understanding, not brevity. Order is the learning path.

units.title: Foundations
units.dek: What the whole thing is made of — before any of the moving parts.

lessons.title: A workbook is one file you can hold
lessons.teaches: The core idea: a whole piece of software — its screen, its logic, its data, its history — living inside a single file you can email, the way you'd email a photo.

lessons.title: The file that remembers how it was made
lessons.teaches: How one file can carry its own source, its own identity, and a complete record of every change — so it explains itself and proves where it came from.

lessons.title: The plain language underneath everything
lessons.teaches: Why everything in a workbook — text, structure, tasks, dates, data — is written in one simple, human-readable format you could read over someone's shoulder.

units.title: Making things
units.dek: How a workbook gets real abilities, and how you drive it.

lessons.title: Giving a workbook real abilities
lessons.teaches: What a toolkit is: taking existing tools and code and safely handing them to a workbook, so it can actually DO things — without ever touching your computer.

lessons.title: When the writing and the program are the same thing
lessons.teaches: How a document can BE the program — the same words a person reads are the instructions the machine runs — and why that makes software you can actually trust.

lessons.title: The one command you type
lessons.teaches: Meet wbx, the single tool you talk to — what it does for you, and why you mostly won't need it to understand any of the rest.

units.title: The engine
units.dek: Where a workbook stops being a file and starts being a living service.

lessons.title: Where a workbook comes alive
lessons.teaches: The Nexus: a workbook on your laptop is a document; plug it into an engine and it becomes a living thing that answers requests, runs on a schedule, and serves other people.

lessons.title: Giving software powers, safely
lessons.teaches: How a workbook gets dangerous-sounding powers — the internet, your secrets, sending messages — without any of the danger: every power is handed over deliberately and can be taken back.

lessons.title: Putting it on the internet
lessons.teaches: What 'deploying' actually means, why it's usually terrifying, and how here it's one push — plus how the live thing keeps a public history anyone can read.

units.title: Agents
units.dek: Software that does work on its own — what that really means, and how to keep it honest.

lessons.title: What an agent really is
lessons.teaches: Strip away the hype: an agent is a loop — it reads, it acts, it looks at what happened, it goes again. Understand that one loop and the rest stops being magic.

lessons.title: Agents that keep working when you're not watching
lessons.teaches: How an agent goes from a thing you chat with to a thing that runs on its own — standing watch, taking shifts, resting between runs, and pausing to ask you when it should.

lessons.title: Knowing whether the agent actually did well
lessons.teaches: The hard part of trusting software that thinks: how you measure whether it did a good job, catch it when it drifts, and keep a record you can't fake.

units.title: Automation
units.dek: Plans that aren't just notes about the work — they ARE the work.

lessons.title: Plans that run themselves
lessons.teaches: Why your to-do list, your calendar, and your project board are all the same thing here — one plain plan that a person reads and a machine carries out, with no copy to keep in sync.

lessons.title: When a plan becomes a program
lessons.teaches: The deeper idea: the same plan that organizes your week can, with no new tools, become an actual running system — and how it changes safely while it's live.

units.title: The disk
units.dek: Where the work lives — a place to keep things that travels with the project.

lessons.title: A place to keep things that travels with the work
lessons.teaches: Every project needs somewhere to keep files. Here that somewhere lives INSIDE the workbook, travels when you send it, and can be asked questions like a spreadsheet.

lessons.title: When the work outgrows one file
lessons.teaches: What happens when a project gets big — reaching out to outside data, remembering things by meaning, and swapping in real storage — without changing how any of it works.

units.title: Trust & sharing
units.dek: How something you can copy infinitely stays trustworthy and safe to share.

lessons.title: Proving where it came from
lessons.teaches: If anyone can copy a file, how do you know a workbook is really from who it claims? The idea of a signature that travels with the bytes and can't be faked.

lessons.title: Sharing without oversharing
lessons.teaches: A file you send is a file you've given away completely — so how do you share the app without handing over the private data inside it? The line between the public shell and the protected core.

lessons.title: Keeping a secret inside a file you hand out
lessons.teaches: The surprising trick: part of a file you give to everyone can be readable only by the one person holding the right key — locked in the open, opened only on permission.

units.title: Under the hood
units.dek: Optional. The why behind the magic, for the curious.

lessons.title: Why none of this is magic
lessons.teaches: A tour, no code required, of how the pieces actually fit — the tiny engine at the center, and the single idea that everything in this whole system is really the same idea wearing different clothes.
